featured_reviews.name: Mamta Kanvinde
featured_reviews.review_text:
Pros:
1. Live counter for laddus. Different experience
2. Different types of bengali deserts that look very rich
3. Chat, namkeens and different types of sweets
4. Exclusive experience where they let you try before you buy

Cons:
1. Costly! It is the most expensive sweet shop i have seen. They offer 6 pieces( literally) for 600 rs whereas you get atleast 1/2 a kg of sweets for that price in a regular sweet shop.
2. They claim that they dont use refined sugar. But they do use other sugars. And sugar is sugar no matter ifs its a fancy sugar or not.
3. They claim their namkeen is healthy because its made in olive oil. But again , oil is oil. At the end it is fried stuff. So using fancy ingredients doesnt automatically make it healthy. This is the kind of false marketing companies use to sell their products.

Thats where my problem lies. You are selling the same stuff that a regular halwai sells but for a good 4x price under the pretext of healthy( which is utter BS). Not cool!

featured_reviews.name: Samira Iqbal
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is my 2nd time ordering from Tharu Sweets. Although I live in Dubai, I had someone who got the mithai for me all the way from Mumbai. The quality of their mithai is topnotch 👌🏽 I've been looking for a mithai place that makes sweets in authentic asli cow ghee since over 10 years now 😅 since I'm quite a foodie with a sweet tooth, but until I taste the motichoor laddoo from Tharu, every other place has been a disappointment. Tharu mithai is the real deal, you can literally taste the ghee and all the mithai is fresh and tastes delish. I've ordered a variety of their sweets- motichoor laddoo, kesar katli, besan laddoo, sohan halwa, mahn ka laddoo and some others that I liked the description of but I forget their names 😂
My only issue is that their online ordering is a bit slow and won't accept international debit cards or even the Indian Bank cards. I had to use my aunt's Indian Bank account to do an online direct transfer.
Final thoughts, I definitely recommend this place for good quality mithai and pricing is reasonable.

featured_reviews.name: Jianna Thakur
featured_reviews.review_text:
Its always been a favorite amongst my family. They have the best of Pure Ghee Sweets.. around here. Its gotten even better since a few years now. They have airconditioned their shop... and their level of hygeine has gone up tremendously too. Sweet and Savoury... all their goodies are great.. but do note that.. the prices are steep too.
The Dal Pakhwan is to die for.. seriously scrumptious..!!
And then their Alu Tikki and chholey is yum too.
Been there since so many years now... but this was the first time that I tasted.. and then bought Mysuru Paak. Its simply the melt in the mouth variant. I have tried it at so many South Indian and Maharashtrian sweet shops... but this is by far the best I've had till date.

Must mention Motichoor Laddoo too. After having the laddoo from regular local mishtaan bhandars here... I had started to hate it.
But Tharu's laddoo.. took me back in time.. straight to the halwai shops at Chowk in Allahabad.. now.. Prayagraj. Fried in Pure ghee and steeped in syrup.. yet one can feel each boondi coming apart in every bite. Rarely does one come across.. such perfectly made laddoos nowadays. Well Tharu's motichoor ladoo.. was almost there. Real Motichoor..!!
You must try.. if you havent already.

Must keep something for my next review. So adieu folks. More after my next visit there..

I purchased 5 samosas from this shop. The staff packed the samosas using their hands and did not inform me that the samosas were cold. Normally, customers expect fresh and hot samosas when buying from a shop.

Very disappointing attitude and poor customer service. I will not recommend this shop to anyone.

featured_reviews.name: Nikhil Aher
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bombay Sweet Shop – A Modern Take on Traditional Indian Sweets

Bombay Sweet Shop beautifully reimagines Indian mithai with a contemporary twist, both in presentation and flavours. The packaging is premium and festive, making it an excellent choice for gifting—especially during Diwali or special occasions. What stands out is the innovation: classic sweets are thoughtfully reinvented with modern textures, balanced sweetness, and high-quality ingredients.

The variety is impressive, ranging from fusion mithai boxes to snackable treats like barks and savoury options. Each item feels well-crafted and fresh, with consistent quality across products. The store itself is vibrant and inviting, and the staff is helpful when it comes to explaining the concept and recommending combinations.

Pricing is on the higher side compared to traditional sweet shops, but the creativity, hygiene, and overall experience justify it. If you’re looking for something unique that still respects Indian flavours, Bombay Sweet Shop is definitely worth a visit—great for self-indulgence and even better for premium gifting.

It’s easily one of my absolute favourites in Mumbai! ❤️

From desserts and chocolates to their food and seasonal specials—everything here just hits right. And their coffee? Truly top-notch.

My personal must-tries:
1.	Gymkhana Cold Coffee Softy with Nut Brittle (pro tip: always ask for extra brittle 😉)
2.	Baked Bhatura with Pindi Chole Hummus – those cherry tomatoes, onions & hung curd dip on the side are chef’s kiss 🤌
3.	Veronicas Cold Coffee with oat milk, date syrup & espresso shots – super smooth and perfectly balanced
4.	Fusion Gulab Jamun Churros with Vanilla Dip – and trust me, order a separate pistachio dip… this combo is next level 🤯
5.	Seasonal Desserts – Peach Matcha Cake, Strawberry Tres Leches & more

Honestly, once you try it, it might just become your go-to spot too!

They also have a great range of souvenirs and healthier options—gluten-free treats, their in-house chikkis (makhana & kurmura), and Indian farsan like bhujia.

✨ Seasonal specials are worth trying too—Ponkh Bhel with Hara Bhara Falafel and Baked Bhatura with Saag Burrata are absolute standouts.

If you're in Santacruz and craving something refreshing and authentic, Banarasi Sweet Mart near the metro station is a must-visit! Stopped by with my friends, and we tried their Lassi and Dahi Bada—both were absolutely delicious!

The Lassi was thick, creamy, and perfectly sweetened, which added to the experience. It was so rich and refreshing that one glass felt like a full meal in itself!
